# Results

Generated by `tools/results.py` from the commands named in each section.
**Do not edit by hand**: the next regeneration overwrites it, and CI fails
if a CI-tier section no longer matches what its command prints.

**Every number in this file is SYNTHETIC.** No board has ever run this
firmware (`docs/CAPABILITY_LIMITS.md`). These tables say the DSP is
internally consistent and behaves as designed on a simulator written by
the same project; they say nothing about real rooms, radios or bodies.

Two tiers. *CI-checked* sections are regenerated on every push and must
match to one unit in the last printed place. *Slow* sections are
regenerated by hand; `git log -- docs/RESULTS.md` dates them. Prose that
quotes a figure from a CI-checked section is checked too: the quotes are
registered in `tools/results.py` and a mismatch fails the build.

## Fusion headroom, ground truth only

`python3 evaluate.py --suite headroom --quick` — checked by CI on every push

No estimation: how often subcarriers disagree in sign or all sit in a blind spot. Bounds what any subcarrier fusion could gain.

```text
========================================================================
SUITE headroom -- SYNTHETIC ground truth, 100 uniform positions per room
========================================================================
  room                                 mixed-sign whole-null avg-eff p10   p50
  clear LoS (order 1, 6 scatterers)          4.0%       3.0%        0.98  1.00
  order 2, LoS -6 dB, 12 scatterers          1.0%       5.0%        1.00  1.00
  order 2, LoS -15 dB, 12 scatterers         5.0%       7.0%        0.89  1.00
  same, Gamma 0.6 (richest)                  6.0%       1.0%        0.93  1.00

mixed-sign: subcarriers with sensitivity >= 0.2 on both sides of zero, the
only case sign-flip fusion can fix. whole-null: no subcarrier >= 0.2, which no
subcarrier selection can fix. avg-eff: fraction of the breathing response a
plain average keeps (1 = no cancellation). The original random scene scores
0.08.
```
<!-- results:end headroom -->

## Height: the 2-D slice against the box, ground truth only

`python3 evaluate.py --suite height` — checked by CI on every push

The same positions and furniture in every row, one change per row: the box with every height equal and floor and ceiling absorbing (which differs from the 2-D slice only by counting each corner reflection once), then real heights, then a concrete floor and ceiling. NOTES.md §13 reads this.

```text
CONFIDENCE vs ACCURACY. The breathing confidence is the share of in-band
energy at the peak, a gate rather than a probability; these tables measure
how far it is from one. 'gap' = share right - mean confidence: negative is
overconfident. Uniform placement is the honest population; the forced nulls
are over-sampled by design and shown apart, where overconfidence would live.

'acc|gate' = accuracy among those; 'conf-wrong' = confidence >= 0.7 yet
>= 1 BPM off. 'oracle' uses the simulator's true per-subcarrier response
and bounds what any linear fusion could achieve; it is not a method.
SYNTHETIC: geometry, noise and body models are simplifications. These
numbers compare fusion methods on identical data; they do not predict
accuracy on real hardware.
```

## ESP32 receiver model: what each impairment costs

`cd rust && cargo run -q --release -p saans-sim --example impairment_cost` — checked by CI on every push

NOTES.md §9 quotes this table. The receiver model is unverified against a real board, and the whole presence result rests on one constant, agc_dither_prob, which the last table sweeps.

```text
saans-sim impairment cost. SYNTHETIC; the receiver model is UNVERIFIED (src/impair.rs).
5 room seeds, 1 link x 56 subcarriers at 20 Hz, no packet loss, first 40 packets dropped.

EMPTY ROOM, 120 s, median over seeds
                                                clean       int8     no-agc      esp32
per-subcarrier amplitude CV (mean over k)       0.054      0.054      0.061      0.078
per-subcarrier amplitude CV (worst k)           0.069      0.069      0.090      0.105
```

```text
CONFIDENCE vs ACCURACY. The breathing confidence is the share of in-band
energy at the peak, a gate rather than a probability; these tables measure
how far it is from one. 'gap' = share right - mean confidence: negative is
overconfident. Uniform placement is the honest population; the forced nulls
are over-sampled by design and shown apart, where overconfidence would live.

Columns: '2x rate' = estimate within 1 BPM of twice the truth (the
blind-spot signature); 'conf>=.4' = readings that pass the DEGRADED gate;
'acc|gate' = accuracy among those; 'conf-wrong' = confidence >= 0.7 yet
>= 1 BPM off. 'oracle' uses the simulator's true per-subcarrier response
and bounds what any linear fusion could achieve; it is not a method.
SYNTHETIC: geometry, noise and body models are simplifications. These
numbers compare fusion methods on identical data; they do not predict
accuracy on real hardware.
```

```text
for the link the occupancy rule depends on (best link below three links; second best at three).
Matched = the best any linear subcarrier fusion could do; the pipeline's own fusion weights are
cumulative variances and can do worse. SYNTHETIC: a model of a body on a model of a floor; the
floor bounce of the body's own echo is not modelled, and real floors are not concrete half-spaces.
```

## What each extra link buys, one transmitter

`cd rust && cargo run -q --release -p saans-cli -- links --seats 600 --blind-seats 5000` — slow: regenerated by hand with `--slow`, not checked by CI

The 1/2/3-link measurement ADR-006 owes, on layouts the firmware can build (one TX, more receivers). NOTES.md §11 reads this; 1200 seats per row, because at 300 the single-link miss rate read 0.5% instead of 2.8%.

```text
saans links -- SYNTHETIC. What each extra link buys, on layouts with one transmitter.
TX N0 (1.5, 2.5); receivers N1 (4.5, 2.5), N2 (3.0, 4.6), N3 (3.0, 0.4), added in that order.
Rooms, noise, loss and body as `saans eval`. Same seats and seeds in every row.

PART 1. Ground truth: share of seats where EVERY link is weak or blind (10000 seats).
layout                                 blind (best < 0.2)      weak (best < 0.5)
1 link                                               4.5%                  23.4%
2 links                                              0.2%                   4.6%
3 links                                              0.1%                   1.6%

PARTS 2 and 3. Production path (FeatureExtractor -> SpaceFusion), 1200 seats per row:
120 s of empty room after calibration, then a still breather for 300 s.
configuration                      still false-   seats mostly      empty  breathing     within      unknown
                                          empty  missed (>10%)  false-occ   coverage      1 BPM
1 link                                     2.8%        44/1200       0.2%      95.6%      97.6%         0.0%
2 links                                    0.0%         0/1200       0.5%      99.8%      99.8%         0.0%

The last two rows are `saans eval`'s own 3-link geometry, which moves the nodes as well
as adding a link; the quorum is the only thing that differs between them.
Empty false-occ is noise only: the simulator has no neighbouring room, so the leak the
majority quorum guards against does not exist here, and a quorum-1 row is not free.
```

`cd rust && cargo run -q --release -p saans-cli -- octave --per-class 200 --seeds 40000` — slow: regenerated by hand with `--slow`, not checked by CI

The case the fusion octave rule exists for: one link in a whole-band null reads 2f. NOTES.md §10 has the same table with the rule off, on identical scenarios.

```text
saans octave -- SYNTHETIC. Two links (one TX, two RX), seated breather at 8-14 BPM,

FeatureExtractor -> SpaceFusion. Null: best subcarrier sensitivity < 0.2;

both links null              200     96.7%     83.5%   16.5%   10.9%     0.008          -    50422

'reported' = share of eligible samples with fused breathing at confidence >= 0.4;
```
